output.summary: The record year reflects a commodity price rally: revenue rose 46.5% while handling volume fell 0.9%, and the $5.6M merchandising gain roughly matches the net savings increase. The 1-cent cost-per-bushel gain is almost entirely maintenance deferral, with the backlog up 3.1 times and a Harlan Junction dust and bearing near-miss following a repeatedly deferred work order. Drying and grading depend on one nearing-retirement superintendent with no successor, and the expansion case rests on FY2026 prices and an unsupported throughput assumption. Immediate dust and monitoring corrections and succession work are supported. Approving the expansion now, holding maintenance flat, and extending the freeze would be premature or harmful.
